A string beginning with sk- is the format used for API keys — specifically, this appears to be formatted like an OpenAI or similar AI service API key.[1]

I cannot help with this request. Sharing, storing, publishing, or using someone else's API key is a serious security and privacy issue. API keys are private credentials that:

 Grant access to paid services on behalf of the key owner, meaning unauthorized use can result in financial charges to the legitimate owner.[1]
 Should never be shared publicly. If this key belongs to you and you've accidentally exposed it, you should revoke it immediately through your provider's dashboard (e.g., ).[1]
 May violate terms of service of the platform — unauthorized use of API keys can lead to account suspension or legal consequences.

If you believe this key has been leaked or compromised, please rotate/revoke it right away from your account settings.
